Instead of asking calmly or telling you how I felt, I assumed things and let that frustration build up inside me. I didn’t say good morning, I didn’t tell you I was awake the whole time, and when we talked, I let that bottled-up feeling come out in my tone. That’s on me.

When I fired back about you not saying anything after “I’m going out,” I wasn’t trying to communicate — I was reacting. I spoke from hurt instead of care, and I understand why that escalated things. I can see now how it made you feel like I was blaming you, when I should’ve just been honest about what was going on in my head.

I want you to know that I wasn’t trying to pick a fight or make you feel bad. I was upset, yes, but that doesn’t excuse being sharp or dismissive with you. You deserve patience, gentleness, and clarity from me — especially when things are already sensitive.

I’m sorry for not saying good morning. I’m sorry for not telling you I was awake. And I’m sorry for letting my tone hurt you when we finally talked. I should’ve handled that moment with more care, because you matter to me.

I’m still learning how to communicate better when my emotions are loud, but please know that my heart was never against you. I care about you deeply, and I hate knowing that my words or tone made you feel otherwise.

Thank you for still talking to me, for listening, and for trying to understand me even when things got messy. I promise to do better — to speak softer, to ask instead of assume, and to remember that we’re on the same side. 

And also I want to speak gently to your heart, because I know it’s been heavy. I know there are moments when you look at us and wonder if you’re enough, or if you’re failing me in some way. I need you to hear this clearly, without doubt or hesitation:

You are not failing me. Not even close baby okay? 

I don’t love you for what you can give me, or for how much effort you manage to show, or for how perfectly you express your love. I don’t love you for consistency, productivity, reassurance, or sacrifice. I love you for who you are — the person you are when you laugh, when you’re quiet, when you’re unsure, when you’re tired, when you’re simply being yourself. That version of you is the one I chose, and the one I continue to choose every day.

If there are times when it feels like I’m giving more, please don’t see that as a burden you need to carry. I’m not keeping score. I’m not waiting for you to repay me or catch up. I give because loving you comes naturally to me. It’s not a chore, and it’s not something I do out of obligation. I do it because my heart wants to, because you matter to me, because choosing you feels right.

I know you worry that you can’t give me what I deserve. But love isn’t about deserving or earning — it’s about choosing, staying, and growing together. We love differently, and that doesn’t mean one love is stronger or weaker than the other. It just means we are two different people learning how to meet each other where we are.

I don’t want perfection from you. I don’t want you to stretch yourself thin trying to be something you think I need. I want you — honest, imperfect, real. I want the quiet moments, the misunderstandings we learn from, the days when things feel easy and the days when they don’t. All of it belongs to us.

Everything is okay my baby. We are okay. Even when things feel messy or unclear, even when emotions run high, I’m still here. I’m not holding your love against you, and I’m not measuring your worth by what you can give me. My heart is calm with you, even when the world feels loud.

So please don’t carry the fear that you’re not enough. You don’t need to be more, or do more, or try harder just to be loved by me. You already are enough — exactly as you are, exactly where you are.

I’m here because I want to be. I stay because I choose you. Always.

Regardless,

120:

121:
Today didn’t really start the way we wanted it to. 
It felt a little off, 
a little tense, 
like something small tried to turn into something more than it needed to be. 

Because somehow, 
even with that, 
we still found our way back. 
(thanks to me) 

We always do. 

And I think that matters more than how things start. 
It’s the way we still choose to soften, 
to come back to each other, 
even after moments that feel a little rough around the edges. 

We even got to sit down and watch a movie. 
The one that just came out. 
And honestly, 
it was really good. 
Better than I expected. 
There were a lot of unfamiliar faces, 
but it didn’t even matter because they all did so well. 
It ended up being one of those movies that’s just easy to enjoy. 

But I'm not here to talk about that. 

I’ve been thinking about why I only ever seem to cry around you. 
And I don’t mean that in a sad way. 
Just in an honest way. 

Because it’s not something I usually do. 
Not with other people, 
not even in my past relationships. 
I’ve always been able to keep things in, 
to stay composed, 
to handle things without letting it show like that. 

But with you, 
it’s different. 

And I’ve been trying to understand why. 

I think part of it is that when we argue, 
when things get tense, 
there are moments where I feel misunderstood, 
not just like we’re disagreeing, 
but like what I’m trying to say isn’t landing the way I mean it, 
like there’s something inside me that I’m trying to express clearly but it comes out differently, 
and somewhere along the way, 
it gets lost. 
And that feeling builds, 
not because I need to be right, 
but because I want to be understood, 
especially by you, 
and underneath all of that, 
there’s this quiet fear that sits there, 
not shouting or demanding attention, 
but always present. 

The thought that after moments like that, 
you might see me a little differently. 
That something shifts, 
even if it’s small. 
That maybe I become a little less of what you want, 
or a little harder to love. 
And even if that’s not true, 
even if you’ve never said anything like that, 
the thought alone is enough to get to me more than I’d like to admit. 

There are also moments where I feel like I’m trying so hard to keep things okay between us. 
Like I’m putting everything I have into fixing things, 
explaining myself, 
holding everything together, 
and still feeling like it’s slipping through my hands a little. 
Like no matter how much I try in that moment, 
it’s not landing the way I hope it would. 

And that’s the part that overwhelms me the most, 
because I’m not used to feeling like that. 
I’m not used to reacting this way, 
to feeling things this deeply in the middle of something difficult, 
but with you, 
everything feels more, 
more real, 
more intense, 
more meaningful. 

And I think that’s what it comes down to, 
the stakes feel higher with you, 
and what we have isn’t something I can just brush off, 
replace, 
or move on from easily. 
It matters to me in a way that runs deeper than I can fully explain, 
and because of that, 
even small things can feel heavier than they should, 
simply because I care that much about us being okay. 

I don’t want to lose you. 

I don’t want small things to turn into something bigger over time. 
I don’t want misunderstandings to slowly create distance between us. 
And maybe that’s why, 
in those moments, 
everything I’ve been holding in just comes out all at once, 
even in ways I don’t always know how to control. 

But baby, 
I want you to hear this gently. 

I’m not telling you any of this to make things heavier between us. 

I’m telling you because you matter to me in a way that makes me want to understand myself better. 
So I can show up for you in a way that feels steady, 
safe, 
and real. 
Not perfect, 
but honest. 
Not overwhelming, 
but consistent. 

I’m still learning these parts of me, 
still figuring out how to hold them better and how to express them without letting them spill over in the wrong moments. 
But I don’t want to do that away from you. 
I want to grow through it with you, 
softly, 
slowly, 
together. 

I love you, my sweet baby. 
Always. 
Regardless.
